headline: Cut the ANET tail, stage two DLR trims, then fund NU and SNOW.
approach: Your core — NVDA, AVGO and VRT — is untouchable here, so the funding has to come from the tail and from DLR, and it does. Sell the sub-2% ANET stub first, then buy NU with those proceeds plus your $210 cash. DLR gets trimmed in two pieces rather than dumped, and only once both trims are done do you put the money into SNOW.
first_move: Sell all $150 of ANET at market today — it is the sub-2% tail your plan wants gone.

steps.sell: Sell all $150 of ANET at market.
steps.why: Clears the sub-2% tail position your plan says to cut first.
steps.realizes: Books a small loss that offsets gains you take; don't rebuy ANET for 30 days.

steps.why: Opens your first financials position, funded by the ANET sale plus your $210 cash.

steps.trigger: DLR gets back to what you paid or better
steps.why: Starts cutting the data-center overweight without selling into weakness.
steps.realizes: Books a small loss usable against gains; don't rebuy DLR for 30 days.

steps.trigger: one week after step 3, with DLR still at or above your cost
steps.sell: Trim $150 more of DLR at market.
steps.why: Finishes the trim in a second piece so you never dump the whole position at once.
steps.realizes: Books the rest of the small loss; you still own DLR, just smaller.

steps.trigger: SNOW pulls back to $256.22 or lower from $273.52
steps.why: Puts the DLR proceeds into a real data position instead of leaving cash idle.

guardrails: Stop all buying for two weeks if the book falls below $8,200.
Never sell NVDA, AVGO or VRT to fund this — core goes only on broken business news.
Skip any buy whose funding sale has not actually happened first.
Do not rebuy ANET or DLR within 30 days or the tax loss is disallowed.

tax.detail: Selling books a loss you can use to offset gains — short-term, which offsets the most expensive gains first. Don't rebuy within 30 days or the loss is disallowed.

governance.thesis: Own a concentrated core of AI compute, data-center power and one great healthcare compounder, bought on weakness and held for years, funded by cutting the sub-2% tail positions rather than adding new cash, with a capped speculative sleeve for the asymmetric shot.
guardrails: No single position above 18% of the book; top five stay under 60%.
Speculative sleeve capped at 8% total, each pick near 3%, never averaged down.
Every speculative buy gets a stop set before entry — SMCI stop $21.
Core names are sold only on broken business news, never on a falling price.
If the book drops below $8,200, pause all new buying for two weeks.
long_term: Core to hold for years: NVDA, AVGO, VRT, GOOGL, MSFT — add on weakness, never sell on price.
LLY is your second engine: 2026 guidance raised to $82-85B and a newly approved weight-loss pill.
Shrink from 15 positions to 8-10 so your best ideas actually move the account.
Keep the power sleeve near 12% through CEG, down 20% this year while signing data-center contracts.
Add Financials — a theme you don't own — only via NU near $14.62, for its fast-growing digital bank.
Hold winners past one year; this year's booked losses offset gains you do take.
